direction_notes: Subjects showing online inhibition (OI+) during TUS-TMS-C had suppressed MEPs with suppressive after-effects at 10-30 min; subjects without online inhibition (OI-) showed facilitated MEPs and no suppressive after-effects.
safety_notes: No participants reported any adverse effects.

timing.protocol_description: Each paradigm included two sets of 30 trials of stimulation separated by 5 min (60 trials total), trials delivered 5 s apart. TUS-TMS-C delivered TMS 10 ms before the end of the 500 ms sonication (0.49 s after onset); TUS-TMS-S delivered TMS 2.5 s after the end of sonication (3 s after onset); TMS only used identical timing with TUS stimulation intensity set to 0 W.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Nineteen healthy subjects were recruited (10 male and 9 female), with mean age of $2 8 . 6 \pm 7 . 2$ years old (mean ± standard deviation, range 21–42 years). Subjects taking medications known to affect cortical excitability, having previous epilepsy history or with implanted devices (e.g. pacemaker) were excluded. All subjects participated in all four study visits that were separated by at least 1 week. Six of the nineteen subjects participated in an additional call-back substudy. The study was approved by Institutional Review Board of National Taiwan University Hospital Hsin-Chu branch (approval number: 108–101-F). All participants provided written informed consent, and the experimental procedures were performed in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki.

source_quotes.randomised: Three different stimulation paradigms were conducted in random order with each paradigm was tested separately at least 1 week apart. Each paradigm included two sets of 30 trials of stimulation separated by 5 min, for a total of 60 trials. The trials were delivered 5 s apart based on our preliminary observation that MEP amplitude gradually decreased when we applied TUS and TMS together for several trials with 5 s inter-trial interval. The three stimulation paradigms were (1) TUS-TMS-C (C = concurrent), (2) TUS-TMS-S (S = separate), and (3) TMS only. In the TMS only condition, the sonication parameters were identical to TUS\_0.5 except that the stimulation intensity was 0 W.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The acoustic intensity profile of the waveform was measured with a calibrated fiber optic hydrophone (HNP-1000; Onda Corp, Sunnyvale, CA) coupled to a preamplifier (AH-2020–100, Onda Corp) and mounted on a customed 3-axis motor system. The hydrophone and transducer were submerged in a tank filled with degassed, deionized, and distilled water. The transducer was excited at the fundamental frequency of 0.5 MHz, focal length of 37 mm, and intensity of 20 W. The oscilloscope measurements of maximum peak voltages per cycle were multiplied by the hydrophone sensitivity (1.211 mV/kPa) to derive the corresponding instantaneous pressure (Pi). The pulse intensity integral (PII) was calculated by squaring the Pi and multiplying it by the inverse of the water density q (997 kg/m3) and speed of sound c (1498 m/s) in the propagating medium (1). From PII, two measures of acoustic exposure can be derived: the spatial-peak temporal average $\left( \mathsf { I } _ { \mathsf { S P T A } } \right)$ , and the spatial-peak pulse average $( \mathrm { I } _ { \mathrm { S P P A } } ) .$ The PII was then divided by burst duration to calculate I<sub>SPPA</sub> (2) and multiplied by pulse repetitive frequency to calculate I (3).
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.pressure_kpa: The focal width at half maximum in the XY plane cross section was 7.52 mm. In the Z axis, the acoustic field generated a near-field peak at 15 mm and a far-field peak at 33 mm (Fig. 3). The peak acoustic pressure (Pi) measured by the hydrophone in the degassed water was 0.612 MPa with MI equal to 0.87.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.isppa_w_cm2: Based on the acoustic pressure field in the water tank, the I<sub>SPPA</sub> and $\mathrm { I } _ { \mathsf { S P T A } }$ of the current protocol were 9.38 $\mathsf { W } / \mathsf { c m } ^ { 2 }$ and 2.81 W/cm<sup>2</sup>, respectively. Since the transducing pressure may have 3.7 to 4.1- fold drop (73 to 76% drop) in intensity with the skull attenuation (Liu et al., 2014), we assumed the pressure was 30% (70% drop) of the original pressure. Therefore, the estimated acoustic peak pressure in the brain target was $0 . 3 ^ { * }$ 0.612 MPa equal to 0.1836 MPa. According to the equation (1), the PII used for calculating I<sub>SPPA</sub> and I<sub>SPTA</sub> would be 0.09 times of the original estimated value. Therefore, $\mathrm { I } _ { \mathsf { S P P A } }$ and $\mathrm { I } _ { \mathsf { S P T A } }$ in the brain target generated by TUS in the brain were $\mathrm { I _ { S P P A } } = 0 . 8 4 \ : \mathrm { W / c m ^ { 2 } , I _ { S P T A } } = 0 . 2 5 2 \ : \mathrm { W / c m ^ { 2 } }$ , respectively. All these values were below the United States Federal Drug Administration (FDA) guidelines for adult cephalic ultrasound with maximum $\mathrm { I } _ { \mathsf { S P P A } }$ of 190 W/cm<sup>2</sup>, $\mathrm { I } _ { \mathsf { S P T A } }$ of $0 . 7 2 \mathrm { W } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ , and a MI below 1.9. No participants reported any adverse effects.

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: A customed two-element annular array ultrasound transducer (H246, Sonic Concepts Inc, Bothell, Washington) was connected to a programmable 0–80 Watt radiofrequency amplifier (Transducer Power Output System, TPO-201–05 Ver. 5.03) with a 50 X impedance matching module. The fundamental frequency was set at 0.5 MHz, with the sonication depth at 37 mm for all experiments. The parameter of the TUS setting was with 1000 Hz pulse repetition frequency, 30% duty cycle, and 500 ms sonication duration. The TUS stimulation intensity was fixed at 20 $\mathsf { W } / \mathsf { c m } ^ { 2 }$ shown on the TPO panel, and the setting was labeled TUS\_0.5.

flags.reason: In-situ pressure/intensity derived by assuming a 30% (70% drop) transmission based on a literature range (Liu et al., 2014), not measured or simulated for this cohort's skulls.
Paper states PRF (1000 Hz), duty cycle (30%) and sonication duration (500 ms) but never states pulse duration explicitly; not computed per protocol.
Paper does not explicitly state whether participants/experimenters were blinded to TUS-TMS-C/S vs TMS-only conditions beyond masking sound.
